rationale: Evidence from iteration 9 (kd 1.0, kp 3.5, base_speed 1.6, sensors y 0.07 at x -0.04 to +0.04, sensor_size 0.012, line_loss last_direction) scored 387.98, the best raced design so far. The oval finished 20 of 20 (mean 1.875 s, progress 0.997). The s-bend improved to progress 0.35 (from 0.30) and the slalom stayed flat at 0.18 (from 0.19). Both bends still end off track with steering_oscillation about 0.19 to 0.20, which is below the 0.25 level the Evaluator flagged as the sign of gain-limited overshoot. Iteration 8 showed that lowering kp alone did not help. The remaining lever, per the Evaluator and the race data, is speed: at 1.6 the robot is still overshooting the tighter bends. Change: controller.base_speed 1.6 to 1.4, the only variable. kd stays at 1.0, kp at 3.5, and geometry and line_loss are unchanged. Expected result: lower speed reduces bend overshoot, so s-bend and slalom progress rise above 0.35 and 0.18, and the score holds at or above 387.98. Oval should still finish, since its mean time of 1.875 s at 1.6 scales to about 2.1 s at 1.4, inside the 3.0 s limit. Risks: the oval finish margin shrinks, and the completion-time term drops slightly. Fallback: if the oval finishes fall below 20 of 20 or the score falls below 387.98, return base_speed to 1.6 with kd 1.0, since that is the best raced design. If the bends still fail with progress at or below 0.35 and 0.18, the next test is kd 1.2 at base_speed 1.4, to see whether more damping helps the slalom. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and controller_errors on all three tracks.
